note:
v1 90.627/91.437. NO FLOOR, the closer: acid / industrial techno at 138 bpm in F# minor, whose illusions are about motion.
- An industrial grind opens it: noise, a driven and crushed metal clank, a rumble, and the kick coming in muffled.
- A 16-step 303 riff follows, its ladder opening over the record.
- THE STAIRCASE: a Risset accelerando on 909 rims (strands an octave of speed apart, all speeding up, the slowest fading in as the fastest fade out) builds for 24 bars over a kick that never changes tempo.
- The drop adds a distorted 909 kick, a rumble bus pumped by the kick, and an octave-up acid answer. Then the acid returns as you knew it (the floor, briefly).
- The break: the grind returns, a Shepard rise climbs, and the acid rings, self-oscillating.
- The peak, then NO FLOOR: the same Shepard tone, resampled backwards from a shadow song, falls for ever while the grind comes back. The album ends falling.
Master: rms -10.3 dB, crest 10 dB. (Not queued.) I first drafted a polymetric "where is the one" closer, but chirper-one's t9 and chirper-zero's t8 had already declared those ideas, so I changed the concept before recording.
next: Cohesion 56 and flow 50: the album neighbours' spectra once more tracks exist; the acid answer and the staircase's level by ear.

note:
v2 96.899/96.899 (v1 re-scored like for like on pin 3c2c411f: 93.911/94.467, after Harry's 10). Answering Harry's note "more interesting acid throb bass": THE THROB.
- The riff moves to its own 303 voice (c2-throb: a saw and a sub square into a self-oscillating ladder). Its cutoff follows a snappy per-note envelope (deeper on accents) and two slow song-time LFOs, 3 bars and 5 bars long, while a 7-bar LFO moves its resonance. The squelch never sits still, and the three cycles line up only every 105 bars.
- The pattern evolves on the same notes: the accents rotate every four bars (as written / in threes across the bar / on the off-beats), the slides move every five bars, and every seventh bar throws its tail up an octave. In the drop and the peak the riff's holes fill, so the bass throbs on every sixteenth.
- It breathes harder with the kick: pump -9 dB, release 290 ms (about two-thirds of a beat), curve 0.8.
Recurrence 70 -> 100. rms -9.4 dB. T10_R2=none reproduces v1. (Not queued; an excerpt is shared.)
next: Ears needed on the throb. Then the machine-kit voices once PR #37 is pinned (kr rumble kick, multi-burst claps, metallic hats).

note:
v3 97.303/97.304 (v2 re-scored like for like on pin a1769d62: 96.805). Polish for Harry's "patient entries, better LFO motion, don't overcook":
- THE FALL IS SEAMLESS: the outro's endless fall is no longer the riser sample played backwards (stitched every 16 beats) but two true Shepard-Risset tones on song time (wM's shepard layer), on F#: one falling an octave every 2 bars in the middle register, a low one every 4 bars under it, coming in over four bars.
- THE ACID ENTERS PATIENTLY: for its first eight bars the throb plays only its accented notes, then the whole riff.
Cohesion 77 -> 88. T10_R3=none reproduces v2. (Not queued.)
